title: Air India Sets Up Full-Time Cost Team as New CEO Tightens Spending After Rs 22,238 Crore Loss
excerpt: CEO Tewolde Gebremariam's October 12 memo creates a cross-functional savings team, routes approvals through the CEO, and launches an employee award for cost ideas.
body:
• Air India has set up a full-time, multidisciplinary cost savings team and tightened spending approvals, CEO Tewolde Gebremariam told staff in an internal message dated October 12.
  • From October 1, approvals are routed through the head of department, CXO and CEO, and a new PRABHAV award will reward employee cost-saving or revenue ideas that are implemented.
  • Air India Group posted a consolidated net loss of Rs 22,238 crore in FY26, more than double the previous year, and has not recorded a profit since returning to private ownership in January 2022.
  • For travellers, the airline says savings will be reinvested in operations and customer experience; no route or fare change was announced in the memo.

Air India has established a dedicated, full-time cost savings team and tightened its spending approval rules as new chief executive Tewolde Gebremariam moves to cut losses at the Tata Group airline. The measures were announced on October 12 in an internal message on the company's Workplace noticeboard, according to Mint, via TradingView, which reviewed a copy of the communication.

"Every rupee we save creates an opportunity to reinvest in areas that matter most, whether it is enhancing our operations, improving our products and customer experience, or strengthening the foundations for our future growth."

- Tewolde Gebremariam, CEO and Managing Director, Air India

What changes inside the airline

Gebremariam, a former Ethiopian Airlines chief who took charge on October 1, succeeding Campbell Wilson, wrote that a multidisciplinary, cross-functional team has been established on a full-time basis to systematically review expenditure and identify savings across functions. Effective October 1, all approvals are routed through the head of department, the CXO and the CEO.

A parallel employee scheme, PRABHAV: The Value Creator Award, will reward staff whose ideas are implemented, covering contract renegotiations, better resource use, procurement improvements, insourcing and waste reduction, according to PTI reporting via The People's Board. Staff On Duty travel approvals now also pass through the same three levels.

The losses behind the drive

Air India Group reported a consolidated net loss of Rs 22,238 crore in FY26, more than double the Rs 10,859 crore loss a year earlier. Air India alone lost Rs 15,368 crore on revenue of Rs 51,452 crore, while Air India Express lost Rs 6,767 crore on revenue of Rs 19,088 crore. Forex losses added Rs 5,033 crore at Air India and about Rs 2,370 crore at Air India Express. The airline has not made a profit since it returned to private ownership in January 2022, and Reuters reported in August that it was seeking about $1.5 billion in additional equity from Tata Sons and Singapore Airlines.

External pressure on costs

The memo cited airspace closures, the West Asia conflict and high jet fuel prices. The closure of Pakistani airspace since April 2025 has forced longer westbound routes, raising fuel, time and crew costs; Wilson had estimated that impact at about Rs 4,000 crore over a year. Delhi aviation turbine fuel prices rose about 13% in October to around Rs 137 per litre, and Air India, Air India Express, IndiGo and Akasa raised fuel surcharges from October 9.

A shift from rebuilding to discipline

Under Wilson, the priority was rebuilding: merging Vistara into Air India and AirAsia India into Air India Express, ordering aircraft and modernising the fleet. Tata Sons has invested Rs 45,347 crore since January 2022, with its board approving in principle a further infusion of more than Rs 10,000 crore. Gebremariam's first town hall on September 28 set the new test: convert that investment into revenue productivity, including revenue per available seat kilometre, while holding safety and reliability. Whether the cost team delivers savings large enough to narrow a Rs 22,238 crore loss will be visible only in the next annual results.
